title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Kampala Signwriting. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Kampala Signwriting
options.lineage: hand-painted school signposts and shopfront boards of Kampala
options.thesis: Every alert is painted like the school's gate signboard: who, which competency, what to do, in stacked flat-colour bands.
options.viewport: Signboard-blue side rail with the school name lettered in condensed caps; dashboard headed by a row of painted alert boards (learner band, competency band in its colour, intervention band), class and competency tallies beside them.
options.risk: Gets loud fast; if every panel is painted, nothing reads as urgent.

raised.raise: Severity is carried by form, not hue alone: one, two or three painted stripes on the board's edge.
A fixed colour language: each of the seven competencies owns one paint colour everywhere; red is reserved for high severity.
Only open alerts are painted at full colour; resolved items drop to ink outline.
Square corners and one-pixel rules throughout, as a signwriter's board has.
One condensed display face on a strict, short size scale, with body text kept quiet.

options.label: Exercise Book Marking
options.lineage: learners' exercise books marked in red Bic
options.thesis: The teacher's red pen does the flagging: circled scores and margin remarks on blue-ruled white.
options.viewport: White workspace with a blue biro top bar; the alert list sits in a standard table where flagged levels are circled in red pen and each row carries a short margin remark.
options.risk: Familiar, and most runs in this category land near it; could drift into ruled-paper costume.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: airport gate boards and segmented boarding passes
options.thesis: The alert list as a live departure board ranked by urgency; a changed row stays lit until the teacher has seen it.
options.viewport: Ranked board of learners by urgency in fixed columns; the learner profile opens as a segmented pass.
options.case: Holds product clarity (a ranking answers who needs help first) but loses on audience identification: few Verona teachers live by gate boards.
options.risk: Reads as transport software; the board metaphor can make learners feel like flights.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: State as line form on a charcoal continuum.
options.viewport: One off-centre rail with every destination as a tick.
options.case: Loses both axes: alien to teachers, and hairlines fail on cheap bright-lit phone screens.
options.kept: Severity carried by form (stripe count), not colour alone.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A fixed colour language with the active course in purple.
options.viewport: Terrain-style overview with the active leg in purple.
options.case: Loses both axes: no map in this product, and contours add noise.
options.kept: One fixed colour per competency, used everywhere.
options.risk: A map with nothing to map.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Coarse pixel display type as the aesthetic.
options.viewport: Poster-scale pixel headline over dense columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: design-school reference, hurts legibility for teachers.
options.kept: One display face on a strict short size scale.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Coded colour strips decoded only for the active item.
options.viewport: A matte black field with one pulse plot.
options.case: Loses both axes: coded labels hide exactly what teachers need to read.
options.kept: Only the active item at full colour; the rest recedes.
options.risk: Mystery where clarity is the job.

options.label: Centre Rail Edition
options.thesis: Two twinned text columns around a vermilion key rail.
options.viewport: A small text block in a wide annotation margin.
options.case: Loses both axes: a reading world on a data-entry screen.
options.kept: Square corners and one-pixel rules, no radius.
options.risk: Bookish costume on a working tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A school analytics dashboard executed cleanly: white cards, slate text, one blue accent.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav, KPI tiles across the top, alerts table below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any SaaS admin template by design.
